sourceNote: Curated, sanitised, offline lexicon compiled from Urban Dictionary and comparable open slang corpora. Pre-processed to drop entries that are primarily hate speech or gratuitously explicit, while retaining culturally significant terms with warnings. Never live-scraped.

entries.definition: No lie, for real — used to stress that something is true.
entries.exampleUsage: That was the best show of the year, no cap.

entries.definition: A lie, or the act of lying.
entries.exampleUsage: He said he ran a mile in four minutes — that's cap.

entries.definition: Charisma, especially skill at flirting or charming someone.
entries.exampleUsage: He walked over and just had unreal rizz.

entries.definition: Mediocre, distinctly unimpressive. Often used dismissively.
entries.exampleUsage: The sequel was mid.

entries.definition: Short for delusional — usually affectionate or self-deprecating about unrealistic hopes.
entries.exampleUsage: I'm delulu about getting that job, but let me dream.

entries.definition: To praise someone excessively or defend them past reason.
entries.exampleUsage: You're glazing him — he wasn't that good.

entries.definition: Doomed, exhausted, or beyond saving.
entries.exampleUsage: I have three exams tomorrow. I'm cooked.

entries.definition: Deeply focused and committed to a task.
entries.exampleUsage: She's been locked in on this project all week.

entries.definition: Perceived coolness or presence; can be gained or lost through behaviour.
entries.exampleUsage: He tripped on stage and lost serious aura points.

entries.definition: Performed exceptionally well.
entries.exampleUsage: That outfit ate.

entries.definition: Is excellent — usually about music or food.
entries.exampleUsage: This track slaps.

entries.definition: Agreement or acknowledgement — 'okay', 'sure', 'you're on'.
entries.exampleUsage: Meet at eight? Bet.

entries.definition: Slightly, quietly, or somewhat — softening what follows.
entries.exampleUsage: I'm lowkey nervous about tomorrow.

entries.definition: Openly and emphatically — the opposite of lowkey.
entries.exampleUsage: I'm highkey excited.

entries.definition: Suspicious or untrustworthy. Popularised by the game Among Us.
entries.exampleUsage: That story sounds sus.

entries.definition: Ending contact with someone abruptly and without explanation.
entries.exampleUsage: We talked for a month and then he started ghosting me.

entries.definition: Giving someone just enough attention to keep them interested, with no intention of committing.
entries.exampleUsage: She's not interested, she's breadcrumbing you.

entries.definition: A romantic connection without defined commitment or labels.
entries.exampleUsage: It's not dating exactly — it's a situationship.

entries.definition: Overwhelming someone with affection and attention early on, often to gain control.
entries.exampleUsage: The gifts every day felt like love bombing.

entries.definition: Manipulating someone into doubting their own memory or perception of reality.
entries.exampleUsage: He kept insisting the conversation never happened — that's gaslighting.

entries.definition: A quirk in a partner that is neither good nor bad, just oddly specific.
entries.exampleUsage: He narrates what the dog is thinking — total beige flag.

entries.definition: A sudden feeling of turn-off toward someone you were attracted to.
entries.exampleUsage: He chased the bus and I got the ick.

entries.definition: Told to someone perceived as too online — go outside, get perspective.
entries.exampleUsage: Arguing about this for six hours? Go touch grass.

entries.definition: Compulsively scrolling through distressing news.
entries.exampleUsage: I was doomscrolling until 2am again.

entries.definition: Content so low-quality or repetitive it feels mentally corrosive; also the state of consuming too much of it.
entries.exampleUsage: That whole feed is pure brainrot.

entries.definition: A one-sided sense of closeness to a public figure or creator who does not know you.
entries.exampleUsage: I had to admit my attachment to that streamer was parasocial.

entries.definition: Living as though you're the protagonist — confident, self-directed.
entries.exampleUsage: She moved cities alone; total main character energy.

entries.definition: Someone acting without apparent thought or individuality, like a background game character.
entries.exampleUsage: He repeats the same three opinions like an NPC.

entries.definition: An exclamation of shock, usually at someone's appearance. From 'goddamn'.
entries.exampleUsage: Gyat, that entrance was something.

entries.definition: Extremely good, typically about food. Originates in Black American vernacular.
entries.exampleUsage: That soup was bussin.

entries.definition: Notably stylish clothing or overall look.
entries.exampleUsage: The drip today is undeniable.

entries.definition: Short for outfit.
entries.exampleUsage: Send me the fit pic.

entries.definition: The greatest of all time; supremely good.
entries.exampleUsage: That album is goated.

entries.definition: When a reply outperforms the original post, signalling disagreement. Also used as a taunt.
entries.exampleUsage: His post got ratioed within an hour.

entries.definition: Admirably true to oneself, unbothered by others' approval.
entries.exampleUsage: Quitting that job was based.

entries.definition: Embarrassing to witness, often through earnestness.
entries.exampleUsage: The speech was a bit cringe.

entries.definition: Bitter or resentful, usually about losing.
entries.exampleUsage: He's still salty about the game.

entries.definition: Shocked or emotionally rattled.
entries.exampleUsage: That ending left me shook.

entries.definition: To show off; also the thing shown off.
entries.exampleUsage: Not to flex, but I finished early.

entries.definition: Evidence — screenshots or records that prove a claim.
entries.exampleUsage: She posted the receipts.

entries.definition: Gossip or the truth of a situation. From Black drag culture.
entries.exampleUsage: Spill the tea.

entries.definition: A subtle, deniable insult. From Black drag culture.
entries.exampleUsage: That compliment was pure shade.

entries.definition: An intensely devoted fan; to be one. From the Eminem song.
entries.exampleUsage: I stan that band.

entries.definition: Someone seen as excessively deferential to a romantic interest. Often used as a jab and sometimes carries misogynistic undertones.
entries.exampleUsage: They called him a simp for defending her.

entries.definition: Restricting who counts as a legitimate member of a community or fandom.
entries.exampleUsage: Quizzing new fans is just gatekeeping.

entries.definition: Deliberately unkempt, self-indulgent, low-effort living without shame.
entries.exampleUsage: It was a goblin mode weekend — snacks and no plans.

entries.definition: Spending long stretches in bed on purpose as rest or avoidance.
entries.exampleUsage: I bed rotted all Sunday.

entries.definition: Hinting at a new relationship online without revealing the person.
entries.exampleUsage: She soft launched him with a photo of two coffees.

entries.definition: Doing only what your job formally requires, withdrawing extra effort.
entries.exampleUsage: After the reorg, half the team started quiet quitting.

entries.definition: Playful, self-aware justification of spending. Often criticised as reinforcing stereotypes.
entries.exampleUsage: I paid cash so it was free — girl math.

entries.definition: Shorthand for a platform's ranking system, often blamed for what one sees.
entries.exampleUsage: The algorithm decided I needed woodworking videos.

entries.definition: Believed suppression of your content without notice or explanation.
entries.exampleUsage: My views collapsed overnight — I think I got shadowbanned.

entries.definition: Social influence or attention, especially online.
entries.exampleUsage: He only posted it for clout.

entries.definition: Seeking attention or association with the famous for status.
entries.exampleUsage: That collab was pure clout chasing.

entries.definition: A private secondary account for a smaller, trusted audience.
entries.exampleUsage: That one's only going on the finsta.

entries.definition: Fear of missing out — anxiety that others are having better experiences.
entries.exampleUsage: Scrolling party photos gave me serious FOMO.

entries.definition: Joy of missing out — contentment at skipping things.
entries.exampleUsage: Stayed home and felt pure JOMO.

entries.definition: Openly announcing a relationship online.
entries.exampleUsage: They hard launched on his birthday.

entries.definition: A sign of healthy behaviour in a person or relationship.
entries.exampleUsage: He apologised without being asked — green flag.

entries.definition: A warning sign about someone's behaviour.
entries.exampleUsage: Checking my phone was a red flag.

entries.definition: Not to be taken seriously — playfully absurd.
entries.exampleUsage: This group chat is deeply unserious.

entries.definition: To talk at length, often without much substance.
entries.exampleUsage: Sorry for the yapping, I'll get to the point.

entries.definition: A difficult experience treated as a necessary part of becoming who you are.
entries.exampleUsage: Getting your heart broken at nineteen is a canon event.

entries.definition: A self-declared phase of life or identity.
entries.exampleUsage: I'm in my rebuilding era.

entries.definition: So immersed in internet discourse that one's sense of proportion slips.
entries.exampleUsage: That take is chronically online behaviour.

entries.definition: An informal read of someone's mood or of a situation's feel.
entries.exampleUsage: Quick vibe check before we go in.

entries.definition: Executed something exactly right.
entries.exampleUsage: The set designer understood the assignment.

entries.definition: Enemies or rivals. Originates in Chicago drill vernacular.
entries.exampleUsage: He won't post the location because of the opps.

entries.definition: Unduly bothered or worked up about something.
entries.exampleUsage: Why are you so pressed about a caption?

entries.definition: Hyping someone up, sometimes past the point of honesty.
entries.exampleUsage: My friends were gassing me before the interview.

entries.definition: A genuinely loyal, dependable person.
entries.exampleUsage: He drove two hours to help — a real one.

entries.definition: Affects you in an unusually strong or particular way.
entries.exampleUsage: That song hits different at midnight.

entries.definition: Diminutive of mental breakdown — used lightly, sometimes masking real distress.
entries.exampleUsage: Had a small menty b over the deadline.

entries.definition: Losing composure and acting impulsively under stress.
entries.exampleUsage: I nearly crashed out in the meeting.

entries.definition: Being present with someone's emotions without trying to fix them.
entries.exampleUsage: I don't need advice, just hold space for me.

entries.definition: A self-declared period focused on recovery and growth.
entries.exampleUsage: No dating this year, I'm in my healing era.

entries.definition: Undermining your own goals, often out of fear.
entries.exampleUsage: Cancelling the interview was self-sabotage.

entries.definition: Sharing heavy personal material on someone unprepared for it.
entries.exampleUsage: I worried I was trauma dumping on a first date.

entries.definition: Making one laugh uncontrollably.
entries.exampleUsage: That reply is sending me.

entries.definition: Abbreviation of 'for real' — sincerity marker.
entries.exampleUsage: That was hard fr.

entries.definition: 'If you know, you know' — signals an in-group reference.
entries.exampleUsage: The third track, iykyk.

entries.definition: 'To be fair' — introducing a mitigating point.
entries.exampleUsage: Tbf, he did warn us.
